basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 19.' and it opens '| Vers. 19. Eme nos in servitutem regiam. Allegorice omnis Aegyptus servus est, et eo'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: | Vers. 19. Eme nos in servitutem regiam. Allegorice omnis Aegyptus servus est, et eo amplius, quo se sponte tradit. Nam filii Israel et ipsi servi fuerant in Aegypto, sed non sponte. Aegyptii vero spontaneam subierunt servitutem, eos utique designantes qui Deum a sua mente excludentes, tradunt se servire immunditiae et iniquitati ad iniquitatem.
